_comment: Declared CI job timeouts, and the policy for deciding when a threshold no
longer matches reality.
Two consumers, deliberately split by whether they need a network:
tests/test_auto_qa_tuning.py runs in the ordinary suite and asserts that
every timeout declared here matches the workflow YAML, in both
directions. That is the half that rots silently, because changing a
timeout in YAML leaves this file stale with nothing to notice.
.github/workflows/nightly-compliance.yml does the half that needs a
network: it re-verifies the published :latest signature against the
committed public key, which nothing else checks after publish time.
The statistic is the MAXIMUM observed duration, not a percentile. A timeout
has to cover the worst run, not the typical one -- a p95 that fits tells
you nothing about the 1-in-20 run that gets killed at the cap.
Duration sampling is deliberately NOT automated. A per-job maximum needs
the jobs API for every run, and a fragile script reporting a number nobody
acts on is worse than a command someone runs when the question comes up.
docs/metrics.md carries that command and treats it the way it treats every
other number here: reproducible, with an honest account of what it is
worth, rather than a collector nobody reads.
This repository does have numeric quality thresholds, unlike its siblings:
the per-module coverage floors in .coverage-thresholds.json. They are
deliberately NOT tuned from here. Raising one is evidenced and the gate
already prints `could raise` when it is possible; lowering one is evidenced
only by an absence, and a deleted test and a removed code path look
identical from the count alone. See tests/check_coverage.py.

_direction: Nothing in this repository rewrites a threshold on a schedule. A bot
adjusting the quality gate on its own would be automating precisely the
decision the gate exists to force. Pinned by tests/test_auto_qa_tuning.py.
_at_risk_ratio: Report when the slowest recent run exceeds this fraction of the timeout.
At 0.75 a job that has grown to three quarters of its cap is surfaced
while there is still room to react, rather than after the first run dies.
_loose_ratio: Advisory only, never a failure. A timeout more than five times the
slowest observed run is not harmful; it just means a hung job burns that
long before the runner reclaims it.

jobs.note: Compiles the ZFS module against the primary kernel. Scales with the OpenZFS release and the kernel; the entry most expected to move.
Scales with the upstream Fedora Kinoite base image.
